stem: On February 20, 1947, Prime Minister Attlee announced the British Government's decision to withdraw from India latest by

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: On 20 February 1947, Attlee stated before the House of Commons that his government intended to transfer power to Indians by June 1948. He also said that if by then no decision on a constitution had been reached, the British Government would have to consider to whom the powers of the central government in British India should be handed over—either to a central government, or to provincial governments in some areas, or in any other manner considered appropriate in the interests of the Indian people. In March 1947, Lord Mountbatten was sworn in as Viceroy. His task was to wind up British power in India. He was specifically instructed to keep India united as far as possible along with the transfer of power; however, he was also authorised to take decisions according to the changed circumstances in India so that Britain could withdraw honourably with minimum loss. Mountbatten soon reached the conclusion during the talks on the transfer of power that the partition of India and the creation of Pakistan had become necessary.

stem: When was the Indian Independence Bill passed by the House of Lords in England?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: On the basis of the Mountbatten Plan, the Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the British Parliament on 4 July 1947. It was passed by the House of Commons on 15 July 1947 and by the House of Lords on 16 July 1947. Thereafter, the Bill received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947.

stem: Who among these headed the two boundary commissions established in 1947 to draw the international borders between India and Pakistan?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: On 30 June 1947, the Bengal Boundary Commission and the Punjab Boundary Commission were constituted. Cyril Radcliffe was appointed as the chairman of these commissions. On the basis of the Radcliffe Award Report, the partition boundaries of Punjab and Bengal were determined, which were later adopted as the India–Pakistan border (and in the Bengal sector, as the present India–Bangladesh border).

stem: The Department of State was established under whose headship?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: Mountbatten announced that after Partition, the issues of the princely states falling in the two new countries—India and Pakistan—would be settled separately by “States Departments.” Nehru entrusted the responsibility of the “States Department” for the integration of the princely states to Sardar Patel. Sardar Patel took charge on 5 July, 1947, and V.P. Menon took charge as his Secretary.

expl: At the time of the Partition of India (transfer of power), J.B. Kriplani was the President of the Indian National Congress. He became President in the Meerut Session in November, 1946, and remained President until November, 1947. After he resigned, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was made the President.

stem: Which of the following political parties was in power in Britain at the time of India's independence?
expl: At the time of India’s independence, Clement R. Attlee was the British Prime Minister. His tenure was from 1945 to 1951. During that period, the Labour Party was in power in Britain. On 20 February, 1947, British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced in the House of Commons that the British would leave India after transferring power to responsible hands, and that this would be done before June, 1948.
